user.title: ASCOM Alpaca Safety Setup
user.description: Add the ASCOM Alpaca Safety monitor to Home Assistant. Safety groups and rules can be configured after setup via the Options menu.

abort.already_configured: ASCOM Alpaca Safety is already configured.

init.title: ASCOM Alpaca Safety Configuration
init.description: Manage safety groups and rules. Saving restarts the monitor: afterwards the settle time of each group applies before it reports safe again (default 300 s, 0 = no waiting).

data_description.group_name: A unique name for this safety group (e.g., Weather, Moon)
data_description.group_logic: OR = any rule triggers unsafe. AND = all rules must trigger.
data_description.settle_time: Time in seconds the group must remain safe before recovery (default 300, 0 = no waiting). It also applies after every restart and after saving the options.

edit_group.title: Edit Group: {group_name}
edit_group.description: Manage rules in this group. 'Save & Close' stores the changes and restarts the monitor; closing this dialog with the X discards them.

delete_group.title: Delete Group
delete_group.description: Are you sure you want to delete the group '{group_name}' and all its rules?

delete_rule.title: Delete Rule
delete_rule.description: Are you sure you want to delete the rule for entity '{rule_entity}'?

rule_entity.title: Rule: choose the entity
rule_entity.description: Group '{group_name}'. Choose the entity this rule watches. The next step lets you watch one of its attributes instead of its state.

data_description.entity_id: The Home Assistant entity to monitor.

rule_source.title: Rule: what does it watch?
rule_source.description: Entity {entity_id}, current state: {current_state}. The rule can watch the state of the entity or one of its attributes, for example the wind speed of a weather entity.

data_description.attribute: The state of the entity, or one of its attributes.

rule_details.title: Rule: when is it unsafe?
rule_details.description: Watching {entity_id}, current value: {current_state}. A rule describes the UNSAFE condition, for example a rain sensor == on.

data_description.operator: Comparison operator for the threshold check. 'Is one of' and 'Is none of' take a list.
data_description.threshold: The value to compare against. Numbers for > < >= <=; on or off for the state of binary sensors, switches and lights; the states of weather entities and of selects are offered; other values are compared without regard to upper or lower case. For 'Is one of' and 'Is none of': a list separated by commas, for example rainy, pouring, lightning.
data_description.unsafe_delay: Ignore brief spikes shorter than this (0 = instant).
data_description.unavailable_delay: An entity that is unavailable or unknown counts as unsafe at once (0). Enter a time to wait for it to come back first: until then the rule keeps its last result.
data_description.watchdog_timeout: Mark unsafe if the entity has not reported within this time (0 = off). Leave empty: 300 s for sensors and weather, off for everything else (binary sensors, switches and helpers only report when they change). Data that is only polled every few minutes (a weather service) needs a time longer than its polling interval.

error.threshold_not_numeric: This operator compares numbers: enter a number as the threshold.
error.threshold_not_on_off: This entity only reports on or off: enter on or off as the threshold.
error.operator_not_for_on_off: This entity only reports on or off: use Equal (==) or Not equal (!=).
error.list_empty: Enter at least one value; separate several with commas (for example rainy, pouring).

missing_entity.title: Safety rule: entity not found
missing_entity.description: The rule in group(s) {groups} monitors {entity_id}, but this entity does not exist or is disabled. The rule reports UNSAFE until you fix or delete it (Settings, Devices & services, ASCOM Alpaca Safety, Configure).
